**Our understanding and proposed approach**

Kilbride Veterinary Group runs three clinics in Navan, Trim and Kells. You have 11 vets and 19 support staff. Your phones are the main pressure point. Around 640 calls come in each week across the three sites. Orla estimates that roughly 38% of after-hours calls go unanswered or land on a voicemail that nobody checks until morning.

Most of those calls are routine. About half are appointment bookings or changes. The rest are repeat prescription requests and questions about whether a situation is an emergency. Emergencies must reach the on-call vet immediately. Orla made clear this is non-negotiable.

You want an assistant that can answer after hours, book routine appointments, send reminders, and route anything that might be an emergency straight to the on-call vet's mobile.

**Proposed approach**

We suggest a 6-week pilot at your Trim clinic. Trim is the smallest of the three sites, so it is a good place to test and adjust before rolling out to Navan and Kells.

During the pilot, the assistant would handle after-hours calls at Trim. It would book routine appointments, send reminders, and pass anything that might be an emergency directly to the on-call vet's mobile.

One important constraint: your practice management system, VetLink 4, does not allow automatic connection to outside systems. This means bookings made by the assistant cannot flow automatically into VetLink 4. We would need to use a daily export/import process, or have staff enter bookings by hand. We recognise this is not ideal. We will look at ways to make the process as light as possible during the pilot.

**Timeline**

You would like the system live before the spring vaccination rush in March 2027. A 6-week pilot at Trim, followed by a phased rollout to the other two clinics, fits within that window.

**To be confirmed**

- Budget. This was not discussed on our call. Orla will raise it with the two partners.
- Storage location for call recordings. We said we would come back to Orla on this. We will confirm in writing before any pilot begins.

**Subject: Hybrid working policy – effective 1 January 2027**

Hi all,

From 1 January 2027, Corrib Engineering is introducing a hybrid working policy. Here is what applies to you.

**Who is eligible**
Any employee whose role can be partly done remotely, as agreed with their line manager. If you are in your first six months (probation), you are not eligible. You work from the office full time.

**Office days**
You must be in the Galway office at least two days a week. One of those days must be Tuesday (team day). Your line manager agrees the second day with you.

**Core hours**
Whether at home or in the office, you must be available between 10:00 and 15:00.

**Getting started**
Hybrid working begins only after both of these are done:

- Your line manager approves it in writing.
- You complete the home-office health and safety self-assessment form.

**Equipment and allowance**
The company provides a laptop and headset. You can claim a one-off home-office allowance of up to €300 against receipts for a desk, chair or monitor.

**What is not covered**
Travel between home and the office is not reimbursed. The company does not pay home utility bills.

**Data**
Confidential client drawings must not be printed at home.

**Review**
The company may review or withdraw hybrid working for any employee or team with four weeks' written notice.

**To be confirmed**
The process for requesting hybrid working (beyond line-manager approval) and how to access the health and safety self-assessment form are to be confirmed.

**Subject: Client portal outage – Friday 14 November**

Dear Client,

On Friday 14 November, our client portal was unavailable for approximately six hours. The issue began at 08:55 and was resolved by 14:55.

A security certificate on the portal expired, causing browsers to block connections. The automatic renewal process had been failing since October. The certificate has now been renewed.

Your data was not at risk. The certificate expiry blocked connections but did not expose any information. Our IT provider has reviewed the logs and confirmed no unauthorised access occurred.

Four clients made uploads between 08:50 and 08:55 that did not complete. Those clients have been identified and will be contacted individually by Monday 17 November to resubmit their documents.

The 14 November ROS filing deadline was not affected. Staff completed the necessary filings for affected clients by phone and email.

We have added monitoring to alert two staff members 30 days before any certificate expires, so this does not happen again.

We apologise for the disruption.

You will run the office day to day. You will supervise our two receptionists. Your duties will include managing the diary system, file closing and archiving, supplier contracts, and liaison with our outside IT provider.

You will also manage the accounts system for client money. We will provide training, but you must be comfortable with numbers and with handling confidential information.

At least three years' experience in an office management or senior administrative role. Legal experience is a plus but is not required.

Monday to Friday, 9:00 to 17:30. One evening a week (Thursday) you will work on reception until 19:00 to cover late appointments. You will get time off in lieu for this.

After a six-month probation period, one day a week working from home is possible.

**Salary and benefits**

€42,000 to €46,000, depending on experience. Pension details are to be confirmed with the partners.

**How to apply**

Subject: Linen contract – what it commits you to

Hi [Name],

Here is a plain summary of what the Brightwash contract asks of you. I am not a solicitor, so please get proper legal advice before signing. A local solicitor who deals with commercial contracts would be the right place to start.

What you are committing to:

- You are locked in for 24 months from 1 March 2025. After that it renews automatically for another year unless you give written notice at least 90 days before the renewal date.
- You must use Brightwash for all linen hire and laundry at the hotel. You cannot use another supplier during the term.
- You must pay for at least 900 kg of laundry each month, even if you use less.
- Your charges go up each year by CPI plus 3%, capped at 8%.

What to watch out for:

- The auto-renewal is easy to miss. If you want out, you need to give notice by around 1 December 2026.
- The minimum volume clause means you pay even in quiet months.
- If Brightwash is late or loses your linen, their liability is capped at what you paid them in the previous 12 months. They are not liable for any loss of business or profits.

Things not stated in the extract that you should ask about:

- Whether there is any way to exit during the initial 24 months.
- How and where to give notice.
- What happens if Brightwash fails to deliver at all.
- What "Premises" covers exactly.

I would not sign this without a solicitor reviewing it first. The exclusivity and minimum volume clauses in particular could cost you if your business changes.

Best regards,
[Name]

**MEMO**

**To:** Managing Director
**From:** [Your name]
**Date:** [Date]
**Re:** CRM replacement – recommendation

**Recommendation: Option B, Larchmont CRM.**

**Annual cost**

| | Pipewell | Larchmont |
|---|---|---|
| Licences (25 users) | €5,400 | €8,700 |
| Xero link (Zapier) | €720 | included |
| **Total per year** | **€6,120** | **€8,700** |

**Why Larchmont**

Gerard has said the Xero link is essential. The accounts team re-keys every invoice today. Larchmont has this built in. Pipewell does not; it relies on Zapier, a third-party connector. If Zapier goes down or changes its terms, the link breaks. We would have no control over that.

Larchmont also handles data migration for us, includes a customs-document template, and offers phone support. These reduce the load on Ciara and on whoever manages the system day to day.

**Trade-offs in favour of Pipewell**

Pipewell is €2,580 cheaper per year. It has no lock-in; we can cancel monthly. Four of six trial users preferred its interface. If the Xero requirement were less critical, Pipewell would be the sensible choice.

**Risks with Larchmont**

The 12-month commitment means we are locked in. If the system disappoints, we pay for the full year regardless. The trial result was not decisive (4 to 2).

**To be confirmed**

- The labour cost of re-keying invoices today, so we can compare it against the €2,580 price gap.
- What happens to our data if we leave Larchmont after the 12-month term.
- Whether the Zapier route for Pipewell has any downtime history or reliability record.

**Next step**

If you agree, I will ask Larchmont for a contract draft and confirm the points above before signing.

Reilly Joinery is a 14-person workshop in Cavan making custom kitchens and wardrobes.

Before we got involved, every quote took about three working days. The owner, Fintan Reilly, priced each job from scratch in a spreadsheet.

We built a quoting template from their last 200 jobs. Standard units and finishes were priced in. We trained the office manager to use it. The project took six weeks and finished in September 2026.

About 70% of quotes now go out the same day. The remaining 30% involve unusual layouts or bespoke finishes. Those still need Fintan and take about as long as before.

Fintan says: "Most quotes go out the same day now. Not every job fits the template, and that's fine - those are the ones that need me anyway."
